# Liquid Glass

> A WebGL2 recreation of Figma's Glass effect. Draw or paste a shape, tune the
> glass, then copy a generated brief that rebuilds the same look on your own
> site. Calibrated against Figma's own Glass panel.

Figma's Glass is a 2D screen-space effect: no 3D, no volume, no light
transport. It displaces and colour-splits the pixels rendered behind a shape.
On a flat background it is invisible, because refracting a uniform colour
returns that colour and splitting it into R/G/B averages back to it.

## Pages

- [Editor](/): the interactive tool. Client-rendered WebGL2 canvas.
- [Guide](/guide.html): full written documentation, algorithm and settings
  reference. Static HTML, no JavaScript required.

## Algorithm

1. Rasterise the shape path to a coverage mask.
2. Height field: Euclidean distance transform of the mask, mapped to a rounded
   rim profile `t = min(dist/depth, 1)`, `height = sqrt(1 - (1-t)^2)`, then
   blurred slightly so the medial axis does not crease.
3. Surface normal from a 3x3 Sobel gradient, with a `tanh` soft-limit on slope
   (`scale = lim * tanh(gm/lim) / gm`, lim ~= 1.35) so thin features cannot
   spike into hard wedges.
4. Refraction: offset the backdrop lookup by `normal.xy * refraction`.
5. Frost and dispersion as TWO SEPARATE accumulations, blended by a rim mask.
   Combining them into one loop tints every frost sample, so raising frost
   paints rainbow rings across the interior instead of blurring.
   - Frost: untinted disc average, golden-angle tap placement
     (`angle = i * 2.39996`), sampled from a mipmap level matched to tap
     spacing so a sparse disc still reads as a smooth gaussian.
   - Dispersion: spectral weights (gaussians centred at 0.0 / 0.5 / 1.0 for
     R/G/B) sampled along the surface gradient, with no frost offset.
6. Chroma restore: spectral averaging pulls toward grey, so keep the
   integrated luminance and scale only the colour difference from it.
7. Composite over the backdrop by coverage.

## Settings

Refraction, Depth, Dispersion, Frost, Splay, Light angle and intensity mirror
Figma's 0-100 sliders one-for-one. Solver internals (rim falloff, normal gain,
chroma, spectral spread, height-field smoothing) are the shader's own units.
Rim falloff, chroma and spectral spread are the three that decide realism.

## Hard-won constraints

- Dispersion is a rim phenomenon. It never appears in the interior.
- Band width and sample count must move together. A wide band with too few
  taps quantises into visible steps.
- Never use per-pixel dithering to smooth the spectral integral; it trades
  banding for visible grain.
- Frost must be a pure blur. If raising it adds colour, frost and dispersion
  are coupled somewhere they should not be.
- Glass carries a baseline blur even at Frost 0, because refraction gathers the
  backdrop over a cone rather than a single ray.
- The effect requires a backdrop texture. Browsers cannot read live page pixels
  from a shader, so supply an image, video frame, or DOM snapshot.

## Presets

Figma default, Frosted card, Prism, Water droplet, Subtle UI glass, Reading
lens, Smoked glass. Presets change glass and solver settings only; shape, size
and background are preserved.
